<user>
Return the next passage of fiction.

I stay at the table long enough to finish my food and hear what the others are planning for the evening.
</user>

summary: **Refining NPC rhymed dialogue and scene flow**
**Planning dinner scene ambiance and spatial cues**

item.text:
You remain at the table as the room empties by degrees, finishing the last of the bread and onions while a server clears the unused settings. He leaves your plate until you set down your fork, neither hovering nor hurrying you.

In the common room, Rashid finds the missing corkscrew in less than a minute. Dena receives it with her splinted hand held pointedly out of the task.

“No practice-group business tonight,” she says.

“Understood.”

“No schedules, petitions, recruitment plans, or speeches about restoring confidence.”

“I had prepared none of those.”

“You’re offended that I think you might have.”

“I’m offended you listed schedules separately from plans.”

One of Dena’s friends laughs. Cards slap onto the low table.

Thessaly pauses beside them with her unfinished pastry. “Which game.”

“Knives,” Dena says.

“I know eight games called Knives.”

“This one permits cheating.”

“Then it has no rules.”

“It has rules governing the cheating.”

Thessaly considers that. “Deal me in.”

A chair scrapes back for her. Rashid begins explaining the scoring until Dena throws a cork at him.

At the dining table, Caelindra tucks her book beneath one arm. “I’m going to the library for the Vauldren travel journals. The complete edition, if this house possesses anything more substantial than excerpts.”

Seraphel rises with her.

“That chapter with innkeepers, mules, and bad ale—  
Read it aloud, and I’ll listen to the tale.”

“You only like the part where his luggage is stolen.”

“The maps are all useless, his mule runs away;  
Your voice makes disaster improve in display.”

“One chapter,” Caelindra says. “And no laughing over the footnotes.”

They leave together through the library door. Seraphel’s warm glow lingers briefly on its dark wood after it closes.

Aldric has already crossed the common room toward the front entrance. Caelindra’s mention of the library brings him to a pause.

“I haven’t taken the annotated Covenant commentary,” he says. “I’ll be in the chapel until second bell.”

No one has accused him of taking it, but he waits a moment before continuing out.

Ysolde stands beside the open garden door. Cold night air gathers around her, carrying the scent of wet stone and year-round flowers.

“The lightning is climbing the eastern side of the storm,” she says. “It should reach the bridge within the hour.”

She steps into the garden and leaves the door ajar behind her.

Ashara is already on her way to the octagon, practice blades over one shoulder, to drill alone.

By the time you finish, the dining hall has gone quiet. Beyond one doorway come cards, complaints, and Dena accusing Rashid of counting discarded suits. Beyond another, a library lamp clicks on. Wind stirs the garden flowers outside.

The server takes your empty plate. For the moment, only you and the seventeen guttering candles remain at the long table.
